item.text: {"chapter_id":"7B","answers":[{"question_id":"7B.1","answer":"The record is mixed but materially adverse. López Obrador made repeated public denials or minimizing statements about Pegasus surveillance and Ayotzinapa-related military obstruction despite investigative and expert evidence pointing to military surveillance, withheld records, and changed accounts (BATCH-0005-E005; BATCH-0009-E006; BATCH-0009-E007; BATCH-0014-E009; BATCH-0026-E019; BATCH-0031-E011). Fact-checkers also classified substantial portions of his government-report and press-conference claims as false or misleading, although the supplied material does not establish that every inaccurate claim was knowingly deceptive (BATCH-0042-E009; BATCH-0043-E009). He sometimes acknowledged facts or ordered investigations, including acknowledging Pegasus use and directing reviews of family-related allegations (BATCH-0005-E005; BATCH-0042-E001). The strongest adverse pattern concerns statements protecting military and political reputation when contrary evidence was available; personal intent and the truth of every disputed assertion remain uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0044-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0043-E009","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0009-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most fact-check evidence predates 2023 or lacks proof of subjective knowledge.","The dossier contains few formal sworn statements, court filings, or international-commitment records personally attributable to López Obrador."]},{"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"Correction and remedy were inconsistent and often inadequate after credible records or investigations exposed error or alleged wrongdoing. López Obrador initially created a truth commission, appointed a special prosecutor, invited independent experts, and ordered cooperation in Ayotzinapa, and he ordered or supported some investigations and acknowledged the Segalmex problem (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0046-E008). However, military agencies withheld or refused documents despite presidential orders, the GIEI withdrew after continued opacity, the missing-person methodology was revised downward amid manipulation concerns, and López Obrador denied or attacked investigators and critics rather than clearly correcting the record (BATCH-0003-E015; BATCH-0008-E002; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0013-E003; BATCH-0013-E011; BATCH-0026-E012). Some CNDH recommendations were investigated or partly implemented, and the State Department reported credible punishment steps in some cases, but these institutional actions do not establish consistent presidential correction or remedy (BATCH-0004-E012; BATCH-0021-R01-E009). Attribution is strongest for his rhetoric, orders, and defense of the Army, but weaker for each agency's noncompliance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0004-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0026-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied record rarely documents a final presidential correction, disciplinary decision, or recovered harm.","Several adverse findings concern institutional resistance rather than proven presidential direction."]},{"question_id":"7B.3","answer":"Formal safeguards existed, but practical separation of family and political interests was weakly demonstrated. López Obrador issued a 2019 memorandum rejecting government business by family members and publicly ordered or supported reviews of alleged conflicts involving his son and Baker Hughes-related contracts (BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0042-E001). Conversely, reports described family residences linked to contractors, relatives and friends receiving government-linked contracts or posts, and the absence of comprehensive conflict-of-interest legislation; López Obrador defended relatives and denied wrongdoing rather than demonstrating recusal, divestment, or independent resolution (BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0007-E002; BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0040-E004). The administrative investigation closed one conflict case for insufficient evidence but acknowledged jurisdictional limits, so it is qualifying rather than exculpatory across all allegations (BATCH-0008-E004). The evidence shows a stated rule and some review activity, but not durable personal compliance or effective firewalling.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0008-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0040-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No complete asset, recusal, divestment, or ethics-disclosure record is supplied.","Most family-conflict evidence is investigative reporting or allegation rather than final adjudication."]},{"question_id":"7B.4","answer":"The candidate index provides substantial evidence of possible family- and network-linked benefit from office, but not a final finding that López Obrador personally enriched himself. Reports identified Pemex contracts connected temporally to his son's residence, contracts allegedly awarded to friends of another son, benefits involving public projects, contracts to a presidential cousin, and irregular procurement including Segalmex and medicine purchasing (BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0007-E002; BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0042-E008; BATCH-0046-E008). The Pío López Obrador investigation was closed by prosecutors for lack of an electoral crime, subject to judicial confirmation, and no evidence supplied establishes presidential personal benefit (BATCH-0005-E003). López Obrador acknowledged or permitted some investigations and removed Segalmex's director, but reassigned him to another government post; recovery and final accountability are not shown (BATCH-0046-E008; BATCH-0006-E007). The material therefore supports a serious network-benefit and accountability concern, while personal enrichment, unlawful intent, and final legal liability remain unproven.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0042-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No asset declarations, tax records, final judgments, recovery orders, or proof of personal presidential receipt of funds are supplied.","Several allegations concern relatives or associates and require explicit knowledge, protection, or benefit to attribute them to the ruler."]},{"question_id":"7B.5","answer":"Appointments and removals show a mixed but concerning preference for loyalty and political control over independently demonstrated competence in some domains. Analytical and investigative accounts describe a governing model favoring loyal, disciplined officials, family-linked appointments, friends of presidential relatives in public contracts or posts, and delayed appointments that impaired autonomous agencies (BATCH-0026-E006; BATCH-0040-E004; BATCH-0018-E015; BATCH-0026-E014). The reassignment of Segalmex director Ignacio Ovalle after major corruption allegations also suggests protection or continued political trust rather than clear accountability (BATCH-0046-E008). Countervailing evidence includes the initial appointment of a respected Ayotzinapa prosecutor and later appointments made after a Supreme Court order, while the State Department reported some effective enforcement actions (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0026-E014; BATCH-0004-E015). The evidence supports recurring patronage or loyalty concerns, but it is not a complete personnel audit and does not establish that every appointment lacked competence or lawful process.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0040-E004","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0004-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The dossier lacks a comprehensive list of appointments, qualifications, removal reasons, and comparative performance outcomes.","Some vacancies resulted from Senate action or shared institutional authority rather than presidential control alone."]},{"question_id":"7B.6","answer":"López Obrador preserved some investigative mechanisms at the outset but progressively weakened or failed to protect independent scrutiny in important areas. He created commissions, authorized archive access, invited international experts, and sometimes ordered agencies to cooperate (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0021-R02-E001). Yet the Army and other agencies withheld Ayotzinapa records despite express orders, the GIEI withdrew, military institutions resisted transparency, INAI was left without a quorum after vetoes and appointment blockage, and autonomous bodies faced budgetary, appointment, or dissolution pressure (BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0013-E003; BATCH-0026-E019; BATCH-0047-E013; BATCH-0026-E020). Courts, the CNDH, journalists, and civil society still exercised meaningful scrutiny, including court invalidation of military and electoral measures, so independent investigation was constrained rather than wholly eliminated (BATCH-0026-E017; BATCH-0031-E013; BATCH-0021-R01-E010). Presidential knowledge of each obstruction is not established, but his defense of the military and support for institutional weakening materially increased the accountability risk.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0026-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0031-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is strongest for institutional obstruction and executive pressure, weaker for direct personal orders to conceal evidence.","The dossier does not provide a complete budgetary or appointment chronology for every oversight institution."]},{"question_id":"7B.7","answer":"The record shows repeated conflict with accountability processes, partial compliance, and significant use of secrecy, political pressure, and public attacks. Presidential or governmental orders existed in Ayotzinapa, but military agencies refused or withheld records; SEDENA failed to comply with an INAI spyware-disclosure order; INAI was impaired by commissioner vacancies; and secrecy exemptions and national-security classifications restricted access (BATCH-0003-E015; BATCH-0004-E013; BATCH-0014-E006; BATCH-0026-E019; BATCH-0047-E013). López Obrador attacked courts, journalists, victim organizations, and investigators when scrutiny threatened the military or government narrative, while the GIEI ultimately withdrew and meaningful remedies remained incomplete (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0030-E012; BATCH-0031-E010). Countervailing evidence includes court proceedings, some government cooperation, CNDH follow-up, prosecutions in selected cases, and the president's formal orders or commitments (BATCH-0004-E012; BATCH-0013-E004; BATCH-0021-R01-E009). The evidence supports obstruction or tolerance at the institutional level and retaliatory rhetoric personally, but not a proven presidential command for every concealed act.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0031-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0021-R01-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Few supplied items are final judicial findings directly against López Obrador.","Some noncompliance was by military or legislative actors whose personal reporting lines and presidential notice are incompletely documented."]},{"question_id":"7B.8","answer":"Promises and implemented decisions show repeated divergence between stated good-faith commitments and later conduct, although some commitments were pursued and some policy changes may reflect genuine priorities rather than deception. López Obrador promised truth for Ayotzinapa and cooperation with investigators, yet the case remained unresolved amid military obstruction and expert withdrawal (BATCH-0003-E015; BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0026-E012). He promised not to spy on journalists or opponents, while investigations identified Pegasus use by military structures; he characterized the activity as intelligence rather than espionage and denied illegal surveillance (BATCH-0031-E011; BATCH-0014-E009). He also promoted transparency and anti-corruption commitments while supporting or tolerating INAI impairment, secrecy measures, selective anti-corruption enforcement, and family-conflict defenses (BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0006-E007; BATCH-0047-E013). Countervailing evidence includes early Ayotzinapa cooperation, formal accountability commitments, social-program and labor reforms, and court-respecting institutional outcomes in some matters, though several outcomes were imposed by courts rather than voluntarily accepted (BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0051-E010; BATCH-0026-E017).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0006-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0048-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not establish subjective intent behind every policy reversal or contested characterization.","Some favorable commitments are institutional or court-driven and cannot be treated as voluntary presidential correction."]},{"question_id":"7B.9","answer":"The record indicates recurring favoritism and privileged access concerns involving family, friends, political allies, and selective enforcement, but direct personal presidential direction is not consistently established. Investigations reported more than 100 million pesos in contracts to friends of a presidential son, contractor-linked family benefits, alleged contracts to relatives and associates, and selective anti-corruption attention toward opponents rather than allies (BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0005-E004; BATCH-0026-E003; BATCH-0019-E019). López Obrador publicly defended relatives, described family matters as their own responsibility, and protected or reassigned politically connected officials, which may support knowledge or tolerance but does not alone prove direction of each transaction (BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0046-E008). Government investigations and some enforcement actions provide contrary or qualifying evidence, including the closure of the Pío case and selected corruption penalties (BATCH-0005-E003; BATCH-0004-E015). The strongest conclusion is a repeated network-access and selective-accountability pattern with unresolved legal findings and uncertain personal benefit.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0042-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The dossier contains no complete procurement, licensing, pardon, or enforcement dataset tied to presidential instructions.","Many reported transactions remain allegations or investigative findings rather than adjudicated corruption."]},{"question_id":"7B.10","answer":"López Obrador's ethical example and institutional legacy are mixed but predominantly adverse. Positive elements include anti-poverty and social programs, formal truth and accountability initiatives, cooperation with some international mechanisms, and selected rights and institutional reforms (BATCH-0015-E016; BATCH-0015-E018; BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0051-E010). Against this, his repeated stigmatization of journalists, defenders, judges, feminists, and critics; defense of the Army amid unresolved disappearances; attacks on independent institutions; family-conflict denials; and tolerance of weak accountability plausibly normalized partisan loyalty, impunity, and distrust of scrutiny (BATCH-0029-E006; BATCH-0031-E010; BATCH-0026-E012; BATCH-0047-E013; BATCH-0012-E009). Independent courts, journalists, civil society, and the CNDH continued to resist and sometimes secured corrective outcomes, limiting the claim of total institutional capture (BATCH-0026-E017; BATCH-0021-R01-E010). The attribution is strongest for presidential rhetoric, institutional proposals, and public defenses; broader violence, corruption, and impunity have multiple causes and cannot be wholly personalized.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0051-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E006","BATCH-0031-E010","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0012-E009","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0021-R01-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Public trust is not directly measured here with a ruler-specific integrity instrument.","Some institutional and violence outcomes are national or inherited and should not be treated as wholly caused by López Obrador."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The most convergent adverse pattern is the combination of presidential defenses or attacks after scrutiny, military and transparency obstruction, and incomplete correction in the Ayotzinapa and Pegasus matters.","Family and associate benefit evidence is substantial but mostly investigative or alleged; the supplied record does not prove López Obrador's personal enrichment or direct order of particular contracts.","Positive evidence concerns formal institutions, initial investigative steps, selected reforms, and some enforcement, but implementation and voluntary acceptance of scrutiny were inconsistent.","Temporal fit is strongest for 2023 institutional conduct, rhetoric, and accountability disputes; many corruption, surveillance, and fact-checking items concern 2019-2022 and function as background patterns rather than isolated 2023 findings.","Country-level corruption, violence, impunity, and human-rights conditions were treated as qualifying context unless the evidence supplied a ruler-specific statement, order, defense, benefit, appointment, or response to scrutiny."]}
